title: AI/ML is becoming a performance factor in motorsport
gist: Ars Technica reports that OpenAI is working with Chip Ganassi Racing and champion driver Alex Palou on car setup optimization, one of several examples of AI/ML becoming an engineering edge in motorsport as tech firms replace tobacco as sponsors.

insights.claim: Motorsport sponsorship has shifted from tobacco and alcohol to crypto, cyber and AI companies because those segments hold an ever-larger share of GDP and the money needed to go racing.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Sponsorship mix is a visible indicator of where corporate marketing budgets are concentrated.

insights.claim: At the amateur level, tech founders including co-founders of GitHub, CrowdStrike and Shopify and the creator of Ruby on Rails raced at the recent Petit Le Mans, replacing dentists as the typical privateer.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Anecdotal sign of tech-wealth flowing into racing.

insights.claim: OpenAI and one of its researchers have worked with Chip Ganassi Racing and driver Alex Palou on optimizing car setups, documented in a YouTube series, beyond a simple sponsorship payment.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Illustrates OpenAI using branded real-world engineering partnerships as showcases for applied AI.

insights.claim: Ganassi is the most dominant team in IndyCar, with 13 championships in two decades, and Palou sealed his fifth title in six seasons in 2026 while winning a third of 18 races, twice as many as anyone else, and eight poles.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Baseline performance means it is hard to attribute gains to AI specifically.
insights.locator: Paragraphs on Ganassi and the 2026 season

insights.claim: General Motors has used AI to predict cautions from radio traffic, one of few LLM applications in motorsport, and built a tool analyzing trackside photographers' crash data within seconds, coordinated from its Charlotte base.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Automakers are using racing as a testbed for applied AI.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'This isn't the first example'

insights.claim: IBM and Dallara published research this year showing AI trained on computational fluid dynamics data can speed up aerodynamic development, something more than one F1 team already does with Neural Concept.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: AI-surrogate simulation for CFD is moving into production engineering workflows.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Earlier this year, IBM and Dallara'

insights.claim: The author suggests the OpenAI partnership adds to an already dominant team's advantage, wondering whether anyone can catch Palou.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: AI advantage compounds on top of existing resource advantages rather than levelling the field.
insights.quote: I wonder if anyone can catch him?
